zin: Welcome to What If, where I take you through history as if you were really there.
Today, you're King Baldwin the Fourth of Jerusalem, the Leper King.
Crowned at thirteen, slowly dying of leprosy, and still the boy who beat the great Saladin.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: You're born in 1161, in Jerusalem, in a Christian kingdom built by crusaders along the coast of the Holy Land.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: Your father, Amalric, is the younger brother of the king.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: When you're two, your uncle dies, and your father gets the crown.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: But the nobles have one condition: he has to leave your mother, Agnes.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: So you grow up in the palace, with a famous scholar as your teacher, William of Tyre.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: One day, you're playing with the other boys, and they pinch each other's arms to see who screams first.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: Everyone screams, except you.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: William thinks you're just tough, until he sees that you can't feel your right arm at all.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: The doctors rub it with oils and give you medicines, but nothing helps.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: Years later, the doctors will finally say the word out loud: leprosy.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: In your time, many people with leprosy have to live apart, outside the city walls.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: But you're the son of the king, so you stay in the palace.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: You learn to ride a horse with your knees, because one hand is already weak.

hoofdstuk: I · The boy who felt nothing
zin: And you're good at it, better than most of the boys who can feel everything.
In 1174, your father catches a fever and dies, at only thirty-eight.
You're thirteen, and on the fifteenth of July, they put the crown on your head.
A boy with leprosy is now the king of Jerusalem.
Everyone knows you won't live long, so the nobles start fighting over who really rules.
The first regent, Miles of Plancy, is stabbed to death in a street in Acre that same autumn.
Then your father's cousin, Count Raymond of Tripoli, rules for you until you're old enough.
Your kingdom is small: a thin strip of land along the sea, with a castle on every hill.
And all around it, one man is building an empire.
His name is Saladin, and he's the sultan of Egypt.
In the same year that you're crowned, he takes the city of Damascus.
Now his lands surround your kingdom on almost every side.
He's more than twenty years older than you, and he has more soldiers than you could ever pay.
Your advisers tell you to stay inside your castles and wait.
At fifteen, you're old enough to rule on your own, and you decide you won't wait.
You send your riders to raid the land around Damascus, right into Saladin's backyard.
Meanwhile, you look for a husband for your sister, Sibylla.
Because a dying king without children needs an heir.
She marries an Italian nobleman, William of Montferrat.
A few months later, he dies of a fever, and she's pregnant.
In November 1177, Saladin marches out of Egypt with one of the biggest armies your kingdom has ever seen.
One chronicler counts twenty-six thousand men.
You're sixteen, your hands are getting worse, and you have about three hundred and seventy-five knights.
You ride to the coastal town of Ascalon, and Saladin's army simply marches past you.
He's heading for Jerusalem, and he thinks you're no longer a threat.
His soldiers spread out to plunder the villages along the way.
So you slip out of Ascalon, and follow them along the coast.
The Knights Templar join you, and so does a hard old warrior called Reynald of Chatillon.
On the twenty-fifth of November, near a hill called Montgisard, you catch Saladin's army by surprise.
His men are scattered, and their own baggage blocks the way.
You charge, and his army breaks.
Saladin himself only just escapes, according to the chroniclers on a fast racing camel.
Of his huge army, only a part ever makes it back to Egypt.
A sick sixteen-year-old has beaten the greatest sultan of his age.
But Saladin doesn't give up, and he's very patient.
You start building a new castle at Jacob's Ford, on the river Jordan, just a few days' ride from Damascus.
In 1179, Saladin comes back and catches your army by surprise at Marj Ayyun.
You're thrown off your horse, and because you can't hold the reins, a knight has to carry you to safety on his back.
A few weeks later, Saladin attacks your new castle before the walls are even finished.
The castle falls, and its defenders are killed or taken prisoner.
You need time, so in 1180 you sign a truce with Saladin.
And at home, the fight over who comes after you gets worse.
Your sister Sibylla falls for a handsome young knight from France, Guy of Lusignan.
Many nobles think he's weak and arrogant, but you allow the marriage anyway.
Raymond of Tripoli can't stand Guy, and your court splits into two camps.
Then Reynald of Chatillon starts attacking Muslim caravans, truce or no truce.
He even sends ships into the Red Sea, toward the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.
Saladin swears that one day he will kill Reynald with his own hands.
In 1182, Saladin invades again, and you ride out to meet him near Belvoir castle.
It's a long, hot fight, and neither side really wins.
But your body is losing its own fight.
You lose the feeling in your feet, and soon you can't walk anymore.
Your hands are wrapped in bandages, and your eyes are slowly going blind.
In 1183, a high fever almost kills you in Nazareth.
So you make Guy of Lusignan regent, to lead the army in your place.
That autumn, Saladin camps right next to Guy's army, the biggest Christian army in years.
Guy doesn't attack, his barons argue, and Saladin simply leaves, plundering as he goes.
When you hear what happened, you're furious.
You take the regency back from Guy, and you crown your little nephew, five-year-old Baldwin, as your co-king.
Guy will not be the next king, you decide, not while you still breathe.
That same winter, there's a wedding at Kerak, a huge desert castle east of the Dead Sea.
Your half-sister Isabella, only eleven, marries the young lord Humphrey of Toron.
Kerak is Reynald's castle, and Saladin finally has him trapped.
His army surrounds the walls, and his catapults hit the castle day and night.
Inside, the wedding party goes on.
According to one story, the groom's mother sends Saladin a plate of food from the wedding.
And Saladin asks which tower the young couple sleeps in, so his catapults can spare it.
It might be a legend, but people still tell it today.
Help can only come from one person, and that person can't walk and can't see.
So your men lay you on a stretcher, and carry you at the front of the army.
When Saladin hears that the leper king is coming, he packs up and leaves.
The next summer, he attacks Kerak again, and again your army marches, and again he leaves.
You're twenty-three now, and you know you're running out of time.
You send the Patriarch of Jerusalem to Europe, to beg the kings there for help.
He even offers the keys of Jerusalem to King Henry the Second of England.
Henry politely says no.
So you make your barons swear an oath: little Baldwin will be king, and Raymond will rule for him.
Guy of Lusignan will not get the crown.
In the spring of 1185, you die in Jerusalem, at just twenty-three.
You never married, and you never had children of your own.
Did you hide your face behind a silver mask, like in the movies?
There's no proof of that at all: the mask comes from a film made in 2005.
What the sources do say is that you kept showing up, until the very end.
Your nephew, the boy king, dies the next year, at only eight.
Your sister Sibylla becomes queen, and she makes Guy king anyway.
It's exactly what you tried to stop.
In 1187, Guy marches the whole army out into the summer heat, to a hill called the Horns of Hattin.
There's no water, and Saladin's army destroys them.
Reynald of Chatillon is captured, and Saladin keeps his promise.
Three months later, Jerusalem surrenders to Saladin.
The kingdom you held together for eleven years falls apart in just two.
Historians still wonder what would have happened if you had lived longer.
You never really won the war, but as long as you were alive, you never lost it either.
More than eight hundred years later, people still call you the Leper King.
A teenager who couldn't feel his hands, and still held off Saladin.
Who should be born next? Tell us in the comments.
